options.content: An expense of the current year not yet paid at the year end
options.rationale: Correct: it is owed, so it is a current liability.

options.content: An expense paid during this year that belongs to next year
options.rationale: That is a prepaid expense.

options.content: Income earned but not yet received
options.rationale: That is accrued income.

options.content: An expense that will never be paid
options.rationale: Accrued expenses are expected to be paid soon.

explanation: An accrual is an expense incurred in the year but still owing at the year end.

stem: How is a prepaid expense shown in the statement of financial position?

options.rationale: Correct: the business is owed a service.
Accrued expenses are liabilities, not prepayments.
The benefit is used within the next year.
It is an asset at the year end and must be shown.

explanation: A prepayment is a current asset: the business has paid for a service it will receive next year.

stem: Which accounting concept requires accruals and prepayments to be adjusted at the year end?

options.rationale: Consistency means using the same methods each year.
Correct: expenses belong to the period in which they are incurred.
Business entity separates the owner from the business.
Money measurement limits records to items with a money value.

explanation: The matching concept matches expenses to the period they relate to, not the period of payment.

stem: Wages paid during the year were US\$7,820. At the year end wages of US\$690 were owing. What is the wages expense for the year?

options.rationale: The accrual was subtracted instead of added.
This ignores the wages owing.
Correct: amount paid plus the amount owing.
This is only the accrual.

stem: On 1 September 2025 a business paid insurance of US\$2,160 for the year to 31 August 2026. Its year ends on 31 December 2025. What is the prepayment at 31 December 2025?

options.rationale: This is the part that belongs to 2025 (4 months).
Not all of it is prepaid; 4 months belong to 2025.
This counts 9 months; January to August is 8.
Correct: January to August 2026 is 8 months.

explanation: 2,160 ÷ 12 = 180 a month; 8 months prepaid: 1,440. The expense for 2025 is 4 × 180 = 720.
hints: Count the months after 31 December 2025 that have been paid for.

stem: A trader forgets to record a closing accrual for electricity of US\$260. What is the effect on the financial statements?

options.content: Profit is understated by US\$260 and current assets overstated by US\$260
options.rationale: Missing an accrual makes the expense too low, so profit is too high.

options.content: Profit is overstated by US\$260 and current assets understated by US\$260
options.rationale: An accrual is a liability, not an asset.

options.content: Profit is correct, but current liabilities are understated by US\$260
options.rationale: The expense is understated, so profit is affected.

options.content: Profit is overstated by US\$260 and current liabilities understated by US\$260
options.rationale: Correct: the expense is too low and the amount owing is missing.

explanation: Without the accrual the expense is 260 too low (profit 260 too high) and other payables are 260 too low.
hints: An accrual adds to the expense and is a liability.

stem: On which side of an expense account is a **closing prepayment** carried down (c/d)?

options.content: Debit side, then brought down on the credit side
options.rationale: That is how a closing accrual is carried down.

options.content: Credit side, then brought down on the debit side
options.rationale: Correct: the balance b/d is a debit (an asset).

options.content: Credit side, then brought down on the credit side
options.rationale: A balance carried down on one side is brought down on the other.

options.content: It is not carried down; it goes straight to the income statement
options.rationale: The prepayment is next year's expense, so it stays in the account.

explanation: The prepaid c/d is on the credit side and the prepaid b/d on the debit side.
hints: A prepayment is an asset at the start of next year.

stem: A closing prepayment reduces the expense shown in the income statement.
explanation: True. Part of the amount paid belongs to next year, so it is deducted.

stem: An opening accrual increases the expense for the current year.
explanation: False. The opening accrual was last year's expense; when paid this year it is deducted from the amount paid.

stem: Match each item with its effect on this year's expense.
explanation: Expense = paid − opening accrual + opening prepayment + closing accrual − closing prepayment.

stem: Complete the year-end journal entry for rent owing of US\$350.
explanation: An accrual increases the expense (debit) and creates a liability (credit other payables).

stem: Telephone charges owing at 1 January 2025 were US\$245. During 2025 US\$4,380 was paid. At 31 December 2025 US\$310 was owing. Calculate the telephone expense for 2025.
explanation: 4,380 − 245 + 310 = 4,445. Adding the opening accrual gives 4,935; ignoring it gives 4,690.
workedSolution: 1. 4,380 − 245 + 310 = 4,445. Adding the opening accrual gives 4,935; ignoring it gives 4,690.

stem: Rudo's business rates were prepaid by US\$520 on 1 January 2025. During 2025 she paid US\$6,240 for rates. At 31 December 2025 rates of US\$780 were prepaid. Calculate the rates expense for 2025.
explanation: 520 + 6,240 − 780 = 5,980. Treating the opening prepayment as an accrual gives 4,940; reversing the closing prepayment gives 6,500.
workedSolution: 1. 520 + 6,240 − 780 = 5,980. Treating the opening prepayment as an accrual gives 4,940; reversing the closing prepayment gives 6,500.
hints: Opening prepayment: paid last year for this year.
Closing prepayment: paid this year for next year.

stem: Sipho pays rent of US\$395 a month for his workshop. By 31 December 2025 he had paid US\$3,950 rent for 2025. There were no balances at 1 January 2025. Calculate the rent accrued at 31 December 2025.
explanation: Due 395 × 12 = 4,740; paid 3,950; accrued 790 (2 months). Giving the rent due for the year (4,740) is the common slip.
workedSolution: 1. Due 395 × 12 = 4,740; paid 3,950; accrued 790 (2 months). Giving the rent due for the year (4,740) is the common slip.
hints: Rent due for the year: 12 months.

stem: Explain why a prepaid expense is shown as a current asset.

points.description: The business has paid for a service it has not yet received / will receive next period
So it is owed a benefit within the next 12 months (other receivables)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The business has paid in advance for a service it will receive next year, so it is owed that benefit; it will be used within twelve months, making it a current asset.

explanation: A prepayment is a short-term right to receive a service.

stem:
Farai runs a furniture shop in Gweru. For the year ended 31 December 2025 his gross profit was US\$48,600. His trial balance included the following expenses (amounts paid):

| Expense | US\$ |
| --- | ---: |
| Wages | 14,250 |
| Rent | 9,100 |
| Insurance | 1,980 |
| Other expenses | 6,340 |

At 31 December 2025: wages of US\$680 were owing; rent of US\$700 had been paid in advance; insurance of US\$495 had been paid in advance.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the wages expense for the year.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the net profit (profit for the year).

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Prepare an extract of the income statement (statement of profit or loss) from gross profit to net profit.

points.description: Insurance 1,485 and other expenses 6,340; total expenses 31,155

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
**Farai's Furniture**

**Income statement (extract)**

**for the year ended 31 December 2025**

points.description: Profit must show the expenses incurred in the year, not the cash paid (matching)
The adjustments add 680 and deduct 1,195, so profit is 515 higher than the unadjusted 16,930

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The income statement uses expenses incurred in 2025 (matching). Owing wages add 680 to expenses and prepayments of 1,195 belong to 2026, so profit is 515 higher than 16,930.

stem: Under which heading in the statement of financial position is an accrued expense shown? (Two words.)
explanation: An accrued expense is a current liability, described as other payables.
